description:
Found while fixing fz-5xp.59.

    extern "C" fn libc::sqrt(float) :: float

The `libc::` here is an fz MODULE PATH. It names where the function lives in
fz's namespace, not where the symbol lives on the machine, and fz has no way to
say the second thing. The runtime therefore has to guess: `fz_extern_symbol_addr`
searches what the process has loaded and then a fixed list of standard
libraries (libm, libc) it opens itself.

That is a stand-in and should be named as one. It works because every foreign
symbol fz names today is in the C standard library. The first declaration of a
symbol in some other library -- libz, libsqlite3, a host's own .so -- has
nowhere to say so and will not resolve.

WHAT IT SHOULD BE: the declaration carries the library, and the runtime opens
that and nothing else. Something like

    extern "C" from "m" fn libc::sqrt(float) :: float

with the AOT link line deriving `-lm` from the same fact rather than hardcoding
it in aot_link.rs, which is the second place that currently knows.

REMOVES: STANDARD_C_LIBRARIES in extern_variadic.rs, and the `-lm` on the
non-macOS branch of link_aot_artifact.
title: A foreign extern declaration cannot say which library it comes from
